title: Millainen and minkälainen: describing one person or thing
summary: Millainen and minkälainen ask what one person or countable thing is like. Millainen talo on? — Talo on pieni.
targetSkills: Millainen and minkälainen: describing one person or thing
objectives: Ask what one person or countable thing is like.
Answer with the appropriate basic-form adjective.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns.
An adjective is a word that describes a quality.
Millainen and minkälainen ask what one person or countable thing is like. They request a description, not its identity or name. These two question words are alternatives in the taught patterns.
keyPoints: A description question asks for a quality, not the thing's name.

sections.title: Answering the question
paragraphs: Describe one countable thing with a basic-form adjective: Talo on pieni (“The house is small”). A short reply Pieni is natural too. The question and answer concern one whole person or thing; substance descriptions have their own later lesson.
A natural short reply to “Millainen talo on?” is “Pieni.” (“Small.”). Use the full reply when it makes the person, action or correction clearer.
To correct a description, reject the incorrect quality and give the actual one. The supplied ei ole does not change the basic adjective form in this one-countable-thing pattern.
The exercises show supporting Finnish words and their meanings when recalling them is not the task. Read the complete English meaning before choosing the question or answer form.
keyPoints: Use the basic adjective form to describe one whole countable thing in these examples.

ei: not; negative verb (marks not and identifies the person). Ei is the singular third-person present negative verb.
ole: be; main verb after the negative verb. After a present-tense negative verb, olla takes the unchanged form ole.
